agent.text: Start here. The coding agent is the AI that wants to pair with a programmer. It works only through a small set of pairing tools, never by touching the editor directly.

relay.text: The relay is the agent's entry point. It receives each tool call, rejects a malformed one, and passes the rest on to the programmer's editor window.

proto.text: The shared protocol is the rulebook both sides follow. It defines what every message may contain, so a bad message stops at the boundary instead of causing trouble deeper in.

bridge.text: The bridge is the editor's front door. It accepts a connection only from a relay that presents the right secret token and speaks the same protocol version.

ctrl.text: The session controller keeps the pairing session's state: whose turn it is, which edits are waiting, and what to report back to the agent.

host.text: The editor host carries out the agent's edits in the real editor at a human pace, so the programmer can follow along. It also runs the side panel for narration and replies.

dev.text: The programmer watches the edits and can step in at any time. An interrupt stops playback at the next safe point, and the agent hears about it in its next report.

speech.text: The agent can also talk. The speech service turns its narration into audio, using a voice model on this computer or a cloud voice service, and tracks whether speech is ready.

companion.text: The audio companion plays that speech on the programmer's own machine. It holds one exclusive claim on the audio output at a time, so two sounds never collide.

native.text: Small platform-specific helper programs make the actual sound on the output device the programmer chose. This is the end of the chain.

call.text: Every pairing session begins when the agent calls a tool. The same few tools cover the whole conversation: start a session, send steps, listen for the programmer, and end.

cwd.text: A start call must name the project folder it works in. The relay refuses a folder that is not a full path or does not exist, and tells the agent why.

disc.text: The relay then looks for the editor window that has this folder open. Each editor window leaves a small note on disk saying where to reach it, so the relay needs no fixed address.

auth.text: The window checks the relay's secret token and protocol version. A mismatch closes the connection and returns an error, so only the right relay can drive the editor.

begin.text: The editor starts a new session, or resumes a paused one from the same folder. Resuming lets a pairing pick up where it stopped.

turn.text: Pairing alternates turns. The agent's turn plays its queued edits; the programmer's turn waits for them to act or reply.

report.text: When a turn ends, the editor sends a report of what happened back through the relay. The agent reads it and decides its next step.

generation.focus: Action Batch Playback — A batch of actions (say, move, select, type, delete, point, run) is validated, rehearsed in memory, queued, and played by the Player at human pace with line identity tracking, programmer interrupts and outside edits, and a BatchResult for each batch.

nodes.label: Rehearse batch in memory on forked line ids
Reject batch with error and code
Playback paused or not agent's turn?
Player performs next action at human pace
Track line identities through each edit
Build BatchResult with status and unplayed
Adopt identities, mark later batches stale

submit.text: The agent sends its edits as a batch: a short list of actions such as move, type, run a command, or say something. Batching lets it plan several moves at once.

schema.text: The first check is shape: does every action have the fields it needs? A malformed batch is refused with a named error before anything touches the editor.

rehearse.text: Next the editor rehearses the batch on a private copy in memory. A batch that would fail, such as editing text that is not there, is rejected up front instead of half-playing in front of the programmer.

queue.text: A batch that passes waits in a queue. It plays only when playback is not paused and it is the agent's turn.

play.text: The player performs one action at a time with deliberate pauses, so the programmer can read each move as it happens. The same code runs the rehearsal and the live playback.

interrupt.text: The programmer stays in control. If they interrupt, or edit the file themselves, the batch stops at the next safe point and the remaining actions do not run.

result.text: Each batch ends with a result: finished, interrupted, discarded, or failed. After an interruption or failure, the agent's next batches are discarded until it has been told what happened.

report.text: The report goes back to the agent. It says what played and what did not, so the agent can re-read the file before it continues.

generation.focus: Narration Speech Synthesis — A spoken `say` is segmented and synthesized through the Kokoro CPU or GPU worker, ElevenLabs or OpenRouter, then tempo-adjusted and sent to an output, with speech-context history, reminders and readiness checks.

nodes.label: Kokoro CPU or GPU worker synthesizes
Play part, hold slot until close

batch.text: Speech is optional. With every batch the agent sends, the editor counts how many have gone by without spoken narration.

remind.text: After three batches without speech, the agent gets a reminder to choose it. The reminder appears only when speech is ready, so the agent is never nudged toward a feature that is broken.

recv.text: When a batch includes text to say aloud, the editor receives that text here.

route.text: Before any synthesis, the editor reserves the audio output. This keeps two voices from playing over each other.

seg.text: The text is split into sentences and spoken one at a time. Short pieces are easier to pause and cancel than one long recording.

prov.text: A voice model on this computer is the default. Cloud voices from ElevenLabs or OpenRouter are the alternative, and they work only on a local desktop.

play.text: Each sentence goes to the audio companion for playback, then the next one starts. The audio diagrams cover that hand-off.

__diagram__.text: This view is a proposed design, not current behavior. Nothing here is built. Green nodes are new, amber nodes change, and unmarked nodes are unchanged context from the Architecture view. The design is in blueprints/ideas/nonverbal-pairing-feedback-design.md (#83).

nv-user.text: Voice and camera have separate opt-ins and separate mutes. Consent text says plainly that derived cues, emotion estimates included, can reach a cloud model. Calibration training and reaction labels need their own opt-in.

panel.text: Draws each owner's snapshot and whether the device is actually open. It owns no camera, speech or session state.

speech.text: Voice mute stays with the narration owner. Text-only narration and programmer-turn observations do not need speech.

nv-lease.text: Sole owner of the helper process. One exclusive lease per active window and session generation; another window gets busy. End, mute, disable, reload, mode change or crash invalidates callbacks, and a reopen waits for confirmed exit. Lost contact is unavailable, not proof the device closed. Cross-window arbitration needs a platform spike and a TLA+ spec first.

nv-helper.text: Child process that owns the camera and models. Emits head pose, face presence, gestures, expression signals and a quality level, each with model, version, units and representation. No frames leave it. Scores are not calibrated probabilities. Four-target support and model licences are unverified.

nv-cal.text: Bounded local store, separately opted in, with retention and deletion controls before first use. A camera, model or display-layout change invalidates the relevant calibration. Per-user trials gate any emotion cue.

nv-layout.text: Known window focus and display facts are kept apart from estimated gaze. Native access, permissions and multi-monitor mapping need a spike. Region estimates can be uncertain or unavailable; never exact gaze.

nv-port.text: New port in packages/core/src/ports.ts. Core labels each observation with what Pair was doing and what the programmer was doing, keyed by batch, or by the programmer turn when there is no batch.

ctrl.text: Owns session generation, activity phase, expiry and replay. A cue never changes turn, playback speed or an approval. Reports carry no wall-clock times. Wake of a pending listen, expiry and canceled-delivery replay need a spec before code; replay never authorizes a second check-in; check-ins are rate limited.

bridge.text: Existing path. The nonverbal field rides the existing report and is not an interrupting event.

relay.text: Renders fixed tentative wording only: no images, landmarks, identity, timestamps, mouse position or other apps. The agent guide gets one rule: explicit words win, a cue never approves anything.

__diagram__.text: This view is a proposed design, not current behavior. Nothing here is built. All nodes are new. Wake, expiry and canceled-delivery replay need a TLA+ spec before code (#83).

open.text: Opens only while opted in, unmuted and in a session. It stays open through pauses, the programmer turn and window blur, so the camera light does not blink.

emit.text: Signals carry model, version, units and representation. No frames, landmarks or identity leave the helper.

quality.text: Missing tracking is unknown. It is never reported as a shake or as disagreement.

label.text: Keyed by batch, or by the programmer turn when no batch exists. Internal time associates and expires cues; the agent sees no wall-clock times. A label appears only when its number crosses an evaluated threshold.

fresh.text: A canceled delivery may replay a cue within the same session. Replay does not authorize a second check-in. A new session never receives old cues.

attach.text: A report field, not an interrupt. A cue never changes turn, playback speed or an approval, and a nod never approves a command.

agent.text: Check-ins are rate limited. Emotion numbers can prompt a check-in or a change of pace but are never stated back as fact about the person.

stop.text: Camera mute or consent revocation discards queued unsent camera cues. Voice mute is independent and does not close the camera.

retire.text: Lost contact is unavailable, not proof the device closed. Recovery must establish retirement before reuse.

comments.text: The relay registers each pairing tool here. `start` checks that the working directory is an absolute path to an existing folder (lines 125-129) before it contacts the editor.

designs.name: Nonverbal feedback during pairing
designs.goal: Let Pair notice conversational feedback such as a nod or head shake from a local camera, without requiring typed or spoken replies.
nonGoals: Recording or retaining video or face images
Approving a command or action from a cue
Changing playback speed or holding playback from a cue
constraints: Opt in explicitly; no camera start while disabled
Frames never leave the local helper
Voice and camera mutes are independent
Missing tracking means unknown, not disagreement
A new session never receives old cues

decisions.text: The agent sees cues only in pair reports; there is no second MCP server
decisions.rationale: Only Pair knows what was shown when, and an MCP server outlives the session

decisions.text: One local lifecycle owner spawns and retires the helper
decisions.rationale: Cancellation is not retirement; a reopen waits for confirmed exit

decisions.text: MediaPipe Face Landmarker and Nodding Pigeon by default; OpenFace is bring-your-own
decisions.rationale: Most emotion and action-unit weights are research-licensed only

assumptions: MediaPipe weights permit the intended use; two model cards still need reading
openQuestions: Does mute carry over between sessions or reset at start?
Is local-only acceptable for the first version?
Can the activity context ship first on its own?
Is Linux arm64 required from the start?

acceptanceCriteria.text: A TLA+ spec of camera lifecycle, physical retirement and independent mutes passes TLC, with each invariant shown to bite
Camera permission, device lease and gaze-to-layout spikes are recorded for macOS and Linux
Code, weight and training-data rights are verified for every model that ships
